observations: The page number «( 11 )» stands at the head of the page, centred. The page has no footnotes and no signature.

L01-L07: the example is two thousand three hundred and twenty-six («duo milia tercentos .xxvi.») by «.ccx.iiiior» (p. 10, L33), 214, set in four places with six in the first, twenty in the second, three hundred in the third and two thousand in the fourth, and below it four under the thousands, one in the place before and two in the third; L07 ends «et hec est figura eorum.», without the figure and without the four points of a gap.

L02 «iiii.or», with a point after «iiii» and «or» raised; L05 «iiiior», without the point. L08: the paragraph begins with the vertical bar that marks the beginning of fol. 105 verso of the manuscript, which the note in the right margin, «car. 105 verso.», names; transcribed as a margin note.
L10: «de super», as two words; L28 «Sic que», as two words (a space of 18 px); transcribed as printed. L11: «succeditur», where L17 has «succedit».

Spaces at punctuation (rule of tools/punct.py: after a mark, a space where the gap is at least 12 px or two thirds of the median word space of the line; before a mark, where it is at least 10 px): L07 «ducenti:et» (9 px, the median word space of the line 15.5 px), L10 «eo,uel», «multiplicatione,scribes» (5 px) and «super.Postea», without a space; with a space before the mark, L12 «similiter ,» (18 px), L24 «ipsum :» (22 px), L26 «differentia ;», L27 «primis ;» and L32 «differentiam ,» (21 px).

Marks not transcribed: light dots at mid-height between words, lighter than the print (darkest pixels 106 to 149, where a printed point is darker than 30): L02 «est» and «in», L32 «eam» and «transire», L33 after «fuerit» and between «uersus» and «dexteram»; L16, a light dot after «que» at the end of the line.
copy_matter: A reader's notes in pencil: «dextra!» in the left margin beside L03, and «secundo (!)» in the right margin; L04, «tres,» underlined and a stroke over «et»; «succedit» in the right margin beside L11, with a stroke over «scribes» and «tur» of «succeditur» marked; L13, a hook at the final «s» of «superioris»; L18, «pur» underlined and «per» in the right margin, and a mark before «reliquas»; L21, a dot between «inde» and «in»; «quod» in the right margin beside L22, L24 and L27, with «uel» underlined (L24) and a stroke over «prima» (L22) and over «et» (L27); L23, a stroke over «unius»; L28, a curve linking «Sic» and «que»; L33, the «e» of «dexteram» marked. Not part of the edition.

critical_notes.evidence: «pur» is not a Latin word; the phrase is «per successiones», by their succession, as on p. 7 («erunt descripte per successiones suas», frame 013, L02); a reader of this copy underlined «pur» and wrote «per» in the margin
critical_notes.impact: none: the sense reads the same
